title: The Man Who Received Tomorrow's Newspaper
logline: A man reads his own obituary, avoids the fire, and learns the paper has already chosen who will pay for it.

source.notes: Original story written for The Midnight Archive. v3 keeps the approved Substitution ending and makes the heater fault and Mara's entry into 4B explicit. No third-party text used.

narration.text: It arrived a day early: his name, his apartment, a fire at 3:07.
He had no subscription. Underneath, in small print: one name per fire.
At 2:40, Elias knocked on 4A. Mara's heater had been sparking all week.
She'd asked him to fix it. He told her to call the super.
He took the stairs and didn't look back.
From the hotel, he watched the smoke rise. At 3:07, 4B burned.
The next paper waited at the front desk. Same fire. Same hour. Different name.
Mara Kwan. Apartment 4A. It said she'd entered 4B to warn him.
Elias laid the two obituaries side by side. His name. Mara's.
The paper wasn't predicting the future.
It was choosing who paid for it.

final_line: It was choosing who paid for it.
visual_style: Sodium amber and ash grey against deep teal-black; one hard practical per scene; 24mm wides, 50mm mediums, 100mm macro details; fine 16mm grain; the newspaper is the only clean white value.
content_notes: Speculative fiction. The newspaper is a fictional device, not a factual claim about prediction, archives or fire safety. The heater is narrative cause, not advice.
